questions.question: GraphQL vs REST — khi nào chọn GraphQL?

options.B: GraphQL: client specify exactly what data needed (no over/under-fetching), single endpoint, strongly typed schema. Best cho: complex data, multiple clients, rapid iteration
options.C: GraphQL thay thế REST hoàn toàn

questions.explanation: REST issues: Over-fetching (GET /users returns all fields even if need only name). Under-fetching: cần nhiều endpoints (GET /user/1 + GET /user/1/posts). GraphQL: single endpoint (/graphql), client requests exactly what needs, schema as contract. When GraphQL wins: complex data graphs, multiple clients (mobile/web/3rd party) need different data shapes, rapid iteration on frontend. When REST wins: simple CRUD, caching (HTTP cache tốt hơn), file uploads, public APIs. REST + GraphQL: dùng cả hai cho different use cases.

questions.question: GraphQL Schema, Query, Mutation, Subscription?

options.B: Schema: type definitions (SDL). Query: read data (like GET). Mutation: write data (like POST/PUT/DELETE). Subscription: real-time updates via WebSocket

questions.explanation: Schema Definition Language (SDL): type User { id: ID!, name: String!, email: String }. Query: query { users { id name } }. Mutation: mutation { createUser(input: {name:'Alice'}) { id } }. Subscription: subscription { onNewMessage(chatId: 1) { content author } }. Resolvers: functions that fetch data for each field. GraphQL server: Apollo Server, Hasura, Strawberry (Python), Ariadne. Introspection: query the schema itself ({__schema { types { name }}}). Playground/Explorer: built-in documentation.

questions.question: N+1 problem trong GraphQL và DataLoader?

options.B: N+1: resolver for each user's posts fires separate DB query. DataLoader: batch nhiều requests thành 1 DB query, cache per request

questions.explanation: N+1 in GraphQL: query { users { posts { title } } } → 1 query users + N queries cho mỗi user's posts. DataLoader (Facebook): (1) Batch: collect all post IDs trong 1 tick → 1 query SELECT * FROM posts WHERE userId IN (1,2,3,...). (2) Cache: same ID trong 1 request → return cached value. Usage: const postLoader = new DataLoader(async (userIds) => { const posts = await Post.findAll({where:{userId:userIds}}); return userIds.map(id => posts.filter(p => p.userId === id)); }). Per-request instantiation (không reuse across requests).

questions.question: GraphQL authentication và authorization best practices?

options.B: JWT trong HTTP header. Auth trong context (không trong resolver). Authorization: directive (@auth), field-level với shield, query complexity limits

questions.explanation: Authentication: HTTP header Authorization: Bearer <token> → middleware validate → attach user to context. Authorization patterns: (1) Resolver-level: if (!context.user) throw AuthenticationError. (2) Directive: @auth(requires:ADMIN) trên field/type. (3) graphql-shield: rule-based authorization middleware (can combine rules with and/or/not). Security: disable introspection in production (không expose schema). Query depth limiting: prevent deeply nested queries. Query complexity: limit max complexity per query (prevent expensive queries). Rate limiting per user.

questions.question: GraphQL performance — identify và fix slow queries?

options.B: Apollo Studio tracing, persisted queries, caching (APQ, Redis), DataLoader, @cacheControl directive, query complexity analysis

questions.explanation: Performance tools: (1) Apollo Studio: field-level tracing, resolver timing. (2) graphql-query-complexity: reject expensive queries. (3) apollo-tracing: timing data per resolver. Fix strategies: (1) DataLoader: batch DB queries (xem trên). (2) Persisted queries: hash → query string, smaller requests, CDN cacheable. (3) @cacheControl(maxAge:60): HTTP cache cho queries. (4) Redis caching: cache expensive resolver results. (5) Federation: split schema across services, each service owns its resolvers. (6) Avoid N+1 với eager loading (DataLoader). (7) Subscription batching: không emit individual events.
